12:6, 14"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"The seven creation days symbolize seven broad eras of sacred or world history, sometimes culminating in an eschatological Sabbath or millennium.","basis":["Genesis 1:1–2:3","Psalm 90:4","2 Peter 3:8","Revelation 20:1–6"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"In many passages “day” is not symbolic at all, but denotes daylight, a calendar day, or an unspecified point in time.","basis":["Genesis 1:5","Matthew 20:2","Acts 20:6"],"prominence":"dominant"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is no single settled symbolic meaning for “day” apart from context. The day–night contrast most recognizably associates day with light, revelation, righteousness, and divine activity, while specialized phrases such as “day of the Lord,” creation days, and prophetic days carry distinct and disputed interpretations.
